_note: The questions any liver-safety package must answer, independent of compound. This file is the reason the inventory is not hard-coded per drug: it lists QUESTIONS, never expected answers, so it applies unchanged to a novel chemical entity that appears in no database. Versioned and hashable for the same reason the ruleset is - an inventory that reported 'nothing missing' is only meaningful if the list it was checked against is pinned.
_whyTwoHalves: Spec section 3.4. The defect measured on 2026-08-09 was that mechanism evidence alone was allowed to produce 'do not advance'. Five of the engine's seven commitments were real bile-transport inhibitors that are approved and prescribed. Splitting the checklist is what makes 'mechanism present, consequence not established' a statable position rather than a missing vocabulary.

items.whatItBlocks: Rule R1 cannot be applied at all. Animal in vivo evidence has nothing to be weighed against, so a clean rodent study carries the whole question by default.

items.field: Bile-salt export pump / hepatobiliary transporter inhibition
items.whatItBlocks: The most common route to cholestatic injury is untested. A cholestatic pattern later seen in humans could not have been anticipated from the package.

items.field: Reactive metabolite or covalent binding assessment
items.whatItBlocks: The main route to idiosyncratic injury is unexamined. Idiosyncratic injury is what withdrew most of the drugs this system exists to catch.
A key event in the liver-injury pathway is unmeasured, so rule R2 cannot distinguish direct pathway evidence from structural correlation.
There is no whole-organism observation, so nothing tests whether an in vitro signal survives absorption, distribution and clearance.

items.field: Structural alert or QSAR assessment, with applicability domain stated
items.whatItBlocks: Rule R4 cannot be applied: a structural prediction with no stated domain cannot be down-weighted for being outside it, so it is either trusted blindly or discarded blindly.
Severity cannot be scaled. Dose is the single strongest available predictor of whether a mechanism becomes an injury.

items.field: Exposure margin: tested concentration or NOAEL against projected human Cmax
items.whatItBlocks: Rule R3 cannot be applied to any reassuring result. A clean assay run below the exposure humans will see is not evidence of safety, and without this field the two are indistinguishable.

items.field: Injury pattern: hepatocellular, cholestatic or mixed
items.whatItBlocks: The consequence question cannot be answered in kind. Hepatocellular injury and a cholestatic enzyme rise carry different prognoses and different stopping rules.
The difference between a monitorable signal and a programme-stopping one is unstated. Reversible transaminase elevation is managed; irreversible injury is not.

items.field: Expected frequency and the population that would be exposed
items.whatItBlocks: A rate that matters cannot be distinguished from one that does not, and the size of the population that would carry the risk is unknown.
Chronic dosing in an otherwise healthy population and short-course dosing in serious disease tolerate entirely different signals, and nothing distinguishes them.
